eval.title: Danaos - A story about investing in shipping stocks!

call.headline_quote: now it looks great but simply not value investing I cannot know where will this be in 2027

reasons.claim: The shipping cycle is extreme and unpredictable, with booms followed by crashes that wipe out retail investors while insiders profit.
reasons.quote: high shipping prices everyone investing in boats usually leads to low prices

reasons.claim: Industry order book to fleet ratio of 20-27% signals a huge coming supply wave that will push prices down like in 2007.
reasons.quote: 20% industry order book to Fleet Rao 27% which means huge supplies deliveries will be coming which means we'll go to lower prices

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: order book to fleet ratio, order book to fleet ratio

reasons.claim: Insider ship owners historically raised equity at boom prices then bought the whole company back at a fraction of that price, meaning retail buyers get sheared while insiders capture the wealth.
reasons.quote: and I would leave it to Greek Danish ship owners if you can't buy back the equity at one six of the price you sold it for in Good Times you are not a shipping investor you are a small retail sheep to be sheared

data_check.gap_note: he says 6, as-of -7.061e+07 (FY2023); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Danaos has long-term charters providing revenue visibility and a well-covered dividend with low P/E, making the current picture look attractive on the surface.
reasons.quote: the stock price it's a little bit down now but the dividend yield is beautiful there 4% the p ratio crazy low 2%

reasons.claim: Management keeps expanding into an oversupplied market and adding debt because they fear looking foolish next to peers, which is the wrong strategic move.
reasons.quote: growing into an over supplied Market is the wrong thing to do but these ship owners keep on doing

data_check.gap_note: trajectory visible at T0; no number stated

external_facts_used: Danaos is one of the largest independent owners of modern container ships
Company history of raising equity in booms (2007, pandemic) and buying back shares/ships in downturns (2009)
Red Sea/Houthi attacks disrupted shipping routes and temporarily boosted prices
Industry order book to fleet ratio of 20-27% (new ship deliveries pipeline)
